findings.source_quote: ὅτι μὴ πλεῖον ἐποιήσαμεν αὐτῶν, ὧν καὶ πλεῖον ἐγνώκαμεν
findings.english_quote: we did not do more than those of whom we also knew more
findings.issue: The second comparative genitive expresses knowing more than those people, not knowing more about them. The draft introduces an unsupported object of knowledge. Its note incorrectly treats the comparative rendering as merely an alternative expansion.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed: “we did not do more than they did, although we also knew more than they did.” Replace the lexical note with an explanation that ὧν supplies the comparison for πλεῖον ἐγνώκαμεν. The revised sentence requires fresh review.

findings.issue: The rendering is contextually defensible, but it leaves the menstrual-separation sense unexplained. In modern English, observing a menstrual period can mean merely monitoring it. The notes do not explain the purity observance intended or the alternatives of menstruation/separation and the menstruating woman.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “to observe menstrual separation.” Add a lexical note explaining the chosen referent and the purity-context rationale, preserving “the menstrual period” and, if the noun is understood personally, “the menstruating woman” as alternatives. This is an interpretive disclosure issue, not evidence of corrupt print.

findings.issue: The draft defensibly takes τιμή as their valuing or honoring of purity, but does not disclose the material alternative “the esteem/value of their purity,” with αὐτῶν attached to ἁγνείας. These readings differ over whether the clause concerns their observance or the valuation of their purity.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a note documenting why the context supports “their honoring of purity” and preserving “the esteem/value of their purity” as an alternative. Do not present the selected attachment as uniquely established.

findings.issue: The supplied edition has an isolated dot before τῆς, but the draft's source_issues records only the two lacunae. The dot has no translated lexical content, yet its treatment should be distinguished from the printed gap markers.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a nonblocking source_issues entry quoting “μετὰ .τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης” and identifying the isolated dot as a supplied print punctuation feature, without alleging an OCR error or proposing replacement Greek. The four-dot and three-dot lacunae are already faithfully retained.

findings.english_quote: baptized me in water as ever-flowing water
findings.issue: The draft retains the relevant vocabulary, but its repeated “water” obscures the construction: ὡς qualifies the phrase εἰς ἀέναον … ὕδωρ. The note says only that the qualification is preserved; it does not explain whether ὡς is taken comparatively or as characterizing the water used.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the more source-transparent proposal “baptized me as into ever-flowing water.” Explain the chosen force of ὡς in a note, preserving the alternative understanding that the springs provided water treated as continuously flowing. Do not add a claim that the water was only apparently flowing. Any replacement requires fresh review.

findings.issue: The draft does not disclose the question mark printed after ἡμέρας. It need not become an English question, and it does not make the surviving phrase untranslatable, but silently dropping this unusual editorial feature leaves the source disclosure incomplete.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a nonblocking source_issues entry quoting “ἡμέρας? τεσσαράκοντα,” recording the supplied question mark without calling it an OCR error or claiming its editorial purpose has been established. Retain “for forty days.” The three-dot lacuna elsewhere in the section is already explicitly preserved without restoration.
